{{Short description|Elements in representations of the symmetric group}}{{No footnotes|date=November 2021}}
In [[mathematics]], the  '''Jucys&ndash;Murphy elements''' in the [[group ring|group algebra]] <math>\mathbb{C} [S_n] </math> of the [[symmetric group]], named after [[Algimantas Adolfas Jucys]] and G. E. Murphy, are defined as a sum of [[transposition (mathematics)|transposition]]s by the formula:

:<math>X_1=0, ~~~  X_k= (1 \; k)+ (2 \; k)+\cdots+(k-1 \; k), ~~~ k=2,\dots,n. </math>

They play an important role in the [[representation theory]] of the [[symmetric group]].

==Properties==
They generate a commutative subalgebra of <math>\mathbb{C} [ S_n] </math>. Moreover, ''X''<sub>''n''</sub> commutes with all elements of <math>\mathbb{C} [S_{n-1}] </math>.

The vectors constituting   the basis of Young's "seminormal representation"   are eigenvectors for the action of ''X''<sub>''n''</sub>.  For any [[standard Young tableau]] ''U'' we have:

:<math>X_k v_U =c_k(U) v_U, ~~~ k=1,\dots,n, </math>

where ''c''<sub>''k''</sub>(''U'') is the ''content'' ''b''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;''a'' of the cell (''a'',&nbsp;''b'') occupied by  ''k'' in the standard Young tableau&nbsp;''U''.

'''Theorem''' ([[Algimantas Adolfas Jucys|Jucys]]): The [[Center (algebra)|center]] <math>Z(\mathbb{C} [S_n])</math> of the group algebra <math>\mathbb{C} [S_n] </math>  of the symmetric group is generated by the [[symmetric polynomial]]s in the elements ''X<sub>k</sub>''.

'''Theorem''' ([[Algimantas Adolfas Jucys|Jucys]]): Let ''t'' be a formal variable commuting with everything, then the following identity for polynomials in variable ''t'' with values in the group algebra  <math>\mathbb{C} [S_n] </math> holds true:

:<math> (t+X_1) (t+X_2) \cdots (t+X_n)= \sum_{\sigma \in S_n} \sigma t^{\text{number of cycles of }\sigma}.</math>

'''Theorem''' ([[Okounkov]]&ndash;[[Vershik]]): The subalgebra of  <math>\mathbb{C} [S_n] </math> generated by the centers

: <math> Z(\mathbb{C} [ S_1]), Z(\mathbb{C} [ S_2]), \ldots,  Z(\mathbb{C} [ S_{n-1}]),  Z(\mathbb{C} [S_n])  </math>

is exactly the subalgebra generated by the Jucys&ndash;Murphy elements ''X<sub>k</sub>''.
